newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa touches new lows on spec selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa touches new lows on spec selling.

text.p: London cocoa futures dipped to new contract lows on Monday, pressured by speculative and trade selling following a large increase in New York longs.
Traders said the 11,000 lot increase in speculative longs in the United States, as reported by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), outpaced market expectations.
"The net longs rose to 20,000 lots. That's a very large number," said one trader, adding that the figures had triggered a wave of selling.
The benchmark March contract scored a new contract low of 954 stg a tonne but closed just above that at 955 stg, representing a loss of nine stg on the day. It saw a session high of 965 stg.
The early session saw a string of trade buying, which traders linked to a fire in a Dutch warehouse on Saturday which destroyed 11,000 tonnes of mainly Ivorian cocoa destined for London.
The main owners were UK trade house Phibro, as well as Dutch grinders Gerkens Cacao and Cacao de Zaan.
"The fire held the market up a bit," said one trader. "Phibro lost the cocoa and they were short of paper so they had to buy it back."

Turnover totalled a moderately brisk 6,276 lots with traders estimating crosses at 1,800 lots and AAs at 300 lots. On the switches, Dec/March widened to 28 stg, March/March was at 68, Dec/May at 42 and March/July at 30, trader said.
Traders and analysts said March could struggle with the 955 stg level before succumbing to downside pressure. They saw further support at 945.
Traders said sterling's strength also contributed to market pressure as origins continued to sell, albeit in modest volumes.
Attentions meanwhile have turned to first cocoa arrivals from the Ivory Coast after the season officially opened last week.
